findings.title: Spawned flusher processes are never killed on hang/crash restart
findings.body: Processes are created via multiprocessing.get_context('spawn').Process, whose SpawnProcess class is not an instance of multiprocessing.Process (both derive from BaseProcess). The isinstance(process, multiprocessing.Process) check at line 254 therefore always fails for the real (non-test) processes, so a hung process is never kill()ed before _create_process_for_shards starts a replacement for the same shards. Two flushers then concurrently call flush_segments/done_flush_segments on the same Redis shards, racing to produce the same segments to buffered-segments (duplicates) or expiring each other's work. The same broken isinstance check at line 346-347 means join() also never terminate()s a hung spawned process. Use multiprocessing.process.BaseProcess (or check for threading.Thread inversely) for these checks.

findings.title: --flusher-processes accepts values that crash or are silently ignored
findings.body: The new click option accepts any int with no validation. Passing a negative value flows through ProcessSpansStrategyFactory into SpanFlusher where max_processes stays negative, num_processes = min(negative, len(shards)) is negative, process_to_shards_map is empty, and 'i % self.num_processes' then raises KeyError/ZeroDivision-style failure while assigning shards, crashing consumer startup. Passing 0 is silently converted by 'max_processes or len(buffer.assigned_shards)' in SpanFlusher.__init__ (line 51) into one process per shard, i.e. the opposite of what the operator requested and a surprising resource jump. Validate the option to be >= 1 (e.g. in the CLI option or SpanFlusher.__init__).

findings.title: Redis memory backpressure double-counts clusters shared across flusher processes
findings.body: submit() sums get_memory_info() over one SpansBuffer per flusher process (lines 298-303). Multiple shard buffers that map to the same Redis cluster each report that cluster's memory, so a cluster shared by shards in different processes is counted multiple times in both 'used' and 'available', while a cluster contained in a single process is counted once. Previously a single SpansBuffer covering all shards could deduplicate by cluster. The weighted used/available ratio is therefore skewed toward whichever cluster happens to be split across more processes, causing the hard backpressure (MessageRejected / pausing the consumer) to trigger too early or too late depending on shard-to-process assignment. Deduplicate memory infos by cluster/service before summing.
